evaluation_result.reasoning:
The claim states that "less than a handful" (i.e., fewer than 5) customers complained about the restaurant's service quality. Let me scan through the dataset to find reviews that explicitly complain about service quality.

1. The review starting with "Big expectations turns into huge disappointment" - extensively complains about rude, condescending service from a male employee.
2. "Honestly just okay place with rude ass workers" - complains about rude service.
3. "Unacceptable service. Called a million times during regular business hours and nobody picked up the phone."
4. "Came here from NYC to try to famous cheesesteak and roast pork sandwich, was disappointed... the service of the workers. All of them should be fired."
5. "While the food is generally good... the service is so bad that it will generally appeal only to tourists..."
6. "Staff here are trying so hard to be cool they forgot to be friendly."
7. "Horrible experience. First timer and didn't know the RULES... Was told to go outside to wait... waited 20 minutes. When I asked about my order I was yelled at."
8. "I like the food but the workers are always so freaking grumpy!"
9. "The food is amazing. I never imagined a time where I would feel compelled to give them a mediocre review... the customer service there can be credited for pushing me to this point."
10. "Staff was rude and the whole place was not organized"
11. "We're in from Chicago... the lady taking our order was as rude as rude can be."
12. "Worst customer service that I have ever seen anywhere!"
13. "If you want a great cheesesteak, Johns is the place to go. If you want great customer service, please avoid at all cost."

There are clearly far more than 5 customers who complained about service quality. The claim that "less than a handful" complained is not supported by the data - it is contradicted by the numerous complaints about service.
